record.paper_title: Non-Supersymmetric (but) Extreme Black Holes, Scalar Hair and Other Open Problems
record.context_brief: Microscopic origin of non-BPS mass in string theory
record.original_question: How should string theory identify the microscopic source of mass for configurations whose Bogomol'nyi bound is not saturated, when the mass is not determined entirely by conserved electric and magnetic charges in the way secondary scalar hair is?

evidence.quote: However, it also looks difficult in string theory to identify the source of the mass when the B bound is not saturated and the mass is not entirely determined by the electric and magnetic charges (just like the secondary hair).
Clearly more work on this area is needed to clarify these crucial issues.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In string theory, charged black hole configurations are characterized by conserved electric and magnetic charges as well as by their ADM mass. For BPS (supersymmetric) configurations, the Bogomol'nyi bound is saturated and the mass is fixed by the charges; the microscopic origin of this mass can then be identified by counting weakly coupled brane/string states carrying the same charges. For non-BPS configurations (including non-supersymmetric extremal black holes), the Bogomol'nyi bound is not saturated and the mass is not entirely determined by the conserved electric and magnetic charges — analogously to "secondary" scalar hair, which is not labeled by an independent conserved charge but is fixed in terms of other data of the solution.

Problem. Provide a microscopic prescription within string theory that identifies the source of the mass of such non-BPS (in particular non-supersymmetric extremal) black hole configurations. Specifically, give a weakly coupled microscopic system (e.g. a configuration of strings, branes, and their excitations) whose mass, computed at strong coupling, reproduces the ADM mass of the non-BPS black hole, and explain which microscopic degrees of freedom account for the portion of the mass that is not determined by the electric and magnetic charges, in a manner parallel to the way secondary scalar hair is determined by the remaining data of the solution.
artifact.category_tag: Non-BPS black holes in string theory
artifact.status_search_result: A general microscopic state-counting derivation of the mass of non-BPS, non-supersymmetric extremal black holes (where the Bogomol'nyi bound is not saturated and mass is not fixed by conserved charges) does not appear to have been fully established. Progress has been made via attractor-mechanism techniques, algorithms generating non-BPS solutions from BPS ones, and partial near-BPS statistical-mechanics treatments, but a complete microscopic identification of the mass source for generic non-BPS configurations remains unresolved in the literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: Microscopic formulation of black holes in string theory
status_evidence.snippet: Review of microscopic state counting for black holes, emphasizing BPS cases and challenges beyond them.
status_evidence.claim: Microscopic state counting is primarily developed for BPS configurations; non-BPS extensions are an active area.

status_evidence.title: The statistical mechanics of near-BPS black holes
status_evidence.snippet: Develops statistical mechanics for near-BPS regimes, indicating that fully non-BPS microscopic descriptions remain incomplete.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses only near-BPS regimes, suggesting the general non-BPS microscopic problem is not fully solved.

status_evidence.title: Extremal Black Holes in Supergravity
status_evidence.snippet: Attractor mechanism for BPS and non-BPS extremal black holes is discussed at the supergravity level.
status_evidence.claim: Non-BPS attractor solutions are constructed, but a microscopic mass derivation is not standardly available.
